newsitem.title: USA: U.S. hearing adjourned for ex-Mexican prosecutor.
newsitem.headline: U.S. hearing adjourned for ex-Mexican prosecutor.

text.p: A judge said Wednesday she would rule in two weeks on a request by the U.S. government to deport a former Mexican prosecutor to his home country.

In a hearing at the Immigration and Naturalisation Service office in Newark, New Jersey, Immigration Judge Annie Garcy set no date for the ruling on the case of former Mexican deputy attorney-general Mario Ruiz Massieu.

After a U.S. district court ruled against the government in February 1996, a federal appeals court last July ordered the resumption of deportation proceedings against Massieu, wanted in Mexico on charges of embezzlement.
On March 15 this year, Massieu was found guilty by a federal jury in Houston, Texas, of taking millions of dollars in bribes from drug traffickers and stashing the money in a Texas bank.
The jury also said that he had not laundered the money and allowed him to keep $1.1 million of a $9 million bank account seized two years ago by the U.S. government.
Massieu was arrested on currency charges in March 1995 at Newark International Airport as he was about to board a plane for Spain with his wife and daughter.

The U.S. and Mexican governments have been trying to extradite him to Mexico on charges he embezzled funds and covered up an investigation into the September 1994 assassination of his brother, Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, a leading member of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party.
In thwarting the extradition efforts, U.S. courts have found repeatedly that there was not enough evidence to support the charges.
In Wednesday's hour-long hearing, Massieu's attorney Cathy Fleming again asked that the deportation order be thrown out on the grounds there was no evidence against Massieu.
The order to begin deportation proceedings against him was signed by then Secretary of State Warren Christopher in December 1995.
